node_definition.done_when: The a-worker-cannot-write-your-home followup f-awcwyh-the-git-shim-refuses-test-fixtures holds. reckon/worker_git_shim.py admits a mutating git verb when the repository it resolves to lies entirely under the run's own scratch directory, /tmp/reckon-crew-scratch followed by the run id. Both the absolute git dir and the git common dir that rev-parse reports must resolve inside that directory. A linked worktree whose common dir lies elsewhere, such as a worktree of a checkout under /home/ITER/mcintos/Code, stays refused. Every other refusal is unchanged. tests/test_git_shim_checks_the_resolved_repo.py gains three cases. 1: with RECKON_RUN_ID set, git init and a commit in a fixture repository under the run's scratch directory succeed. 2: a commit into a synthesised foreign checkout outside the scratch directory is still refused, and its HEAD is unchanged. 3: a linked worktree placed under the scratch directory, whose common dir lies in a synthesised checkout outside it, is refused, and that checkout's refs are unchanged. Each case runs its git commands in a child process group under a 60 s timeout, with two shim directories on PATH. A declared negative control is executed and logged under pytest: admitting on the toplevel alone turns case 3 red. The node gate is that test file at head, ending EXIT=0. Every log sits under the run directory, headed with revision, tree and literal command, and ends EXIT=. Only reckon/worker_git_shim.py and that test file change.
